theory.intro: Once a dataset is ordered, three features often stand out at a glance. A **cluster** is a group of values bunched closely together, a **gap** is an interval containing no data at all, and an **outlier** is a single value that sits much higher or much lower than the rest. You identify all three **informally**, by looking at how the values are spaced — no calculation is needed.
facts: A **cluster** is a group of data values grouped closely around each other. A dataset can contain more than one cluster.
A **gap** is an interval that contains no data values. Describe it by naming the two values it lies between.
An **outlier** is a data value **much higher or much lower** than all the others, so it stands alone.
The largest value is **not** automatically an outlier. It is an outlier only when it sits far from the next value.
A wide spread does not create an outlier: values spaced evenly across a large interval have no value far from the rest.
Ordering the data first makes every cluster, gap and outlier easy to see.
steps: Order the data values from smallest to largest
Identify any value far from all the others (an outlier)
Identify any interval with no data values (a gap)
Identify any group of values bunched closely together (a cluster)

foundation.question_text: The heights, in metres, of six trees in a park are $4.2$, $3.8$, $4.5$, $12.6$, $4.0$ and $3.9$. Which height is the outlier?
foundation.solution_text:
$3.8, 3.9, 4.0, 4.2, 4.5, 12.6$
The outlier is $12.6$ m, because it is much higher than every other height.

foundation.question_text: The daily maximum temperature, in $^{\circ}$C, was recorded for seven days: $29$, $31$, $30$, $12$, $28$, $32$, $30$. Which temperature is the outlier?
foundation.solution_text:
$12, 28, 29, 30, 30, 31, 32$
The outlier is $12^{\circ}$C, because it is much lower than every other temperature.

$5, 6, 7, 8, 15$
The outlier is $15$ m, because it is much higher than the other four heights.

foundation.question_text: The daily maximum temperature, in $^{\circ}$C, was recorded for eight days: $18$, $19$, $20$, $20$, $21$, $25$, $29$, $33$. Describe the cluster in this dataset.
foundation.solution_text:
$18, 19, 20, 20, 21, 25, 29, 33$
Five of the eight temperatures lie between $18^{\circ}$C and $21^{\circ}$C, so there is a cluster from $18^{\circ}$C to $21^{\circ}$C.

foundation.question_text: The prices of six houses in a street, in thousands of dollars, are $540$, $560$, $580$, $600$, $750$ and $770$. Between which two prices is there a gap?
foundation.solution_text:
$540, 560, 580, 600, 750, 770$
There is a gap between $600$ and $750$, because no house is priced in that interval.

foundation.question_text: The heights, in metres, of six trees in a park are $6.1$, $5.4$, $7.0$, $6.6$, $5.9$ and $7.3$. Does this dataset contain an outlier? Explain your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
$5.4, 5.9, 6.1, 6.6, 7.0, 7.3$
No. Every height lies between $5.4$ m and $7.3$ m, and each height is at most $0.5$ m from the next one, so no height sits far from the rest.

$16, 28, 28, 30, 30, 32$
The outlier is $16^{\circ}$C, recorded on Thursday, because it is much lower than the other five temperatures.

$260, 270, 280, 290, 380, 390, 400$
There is a gap between $290$ and $380$, because no unit is priced in that interval.

development.question_text: The heights, in metres, of six trees in a park are $1.2$, $7.8$, $8.1$, $8.4$, $8.6$ and $9.0$. Which height is the outlier?
development.solution_text:
$1.2, 7.8, 8.1, 8.4, 8.6, 9.0$
The outlier is $1.2$ m, because it is much lower than every other height.
The largest height, $9.0$ m, is only $0.4$ m above the next one, so it is not an outlier.

$520, 550, 580, 600, 850, 880$
There is a cluster of four prices from $520$ to $600$, and a second cluster of two prices from $850$ to $880$.
There is a gap between $600$ and $850$, because no house is priced in that interval.

development.question_text: The daily maximum temperature, in $^{\circ}$C, was recorded for ten days: $23$, $24$, $22$, $25$, $24$, $38$, $23$, $26$, $25$, $24$. State the outlier and the gap in this dataset.
development.solution_text:
$22, 23, 23, 24, 24, 24, 25, 25, 26, 38$
The outlier is $38^{\circ}$C, because it is much higher than every other temperature.
There is a gap between $26^{\circ}$C and $38^{\circ}$C, because no temperature was recorded in that interval.

development.question_text: The prices of six houses in a street, in thousands of dollars, are $420$, $480$, $540$, $600$, $660$ and $720$. Ben says that $720$ must be an outlier because the prices are spread over $300$ thousand dollars. Is Ben correct? Explain your answer.
development.solution_text:
$420, 480, 540, 600, 660, 720$
No. Each price is exactly $60$ more than the one before, so no price sits far from the rest.
A wide spread on its own does not create an outlier — an outlier must be much higher or much lower than the other values.

development.question_text: The heights, in metres, of seven trees in a park are $2.1$, $2.4$, $2.6$, $2.8$, $6.9$, $7.2$ and $7.4$. Between which two heights is there a gap?
development.solution_text:
$2.1, 2.4, 2.6, 2.8, 6.9, 7.2, 7.4$
There is a gap between $2.8$ m and $6.9$ m, because no tree has a height in that interval.

development.question_text:
Units in two blocks are for sale. The prices, in thousands of dollars, are:
Block A: $305$, $320$, $340$, $355$, $370$, $390$
Block B: $312$, $318$, $325$, $331$, $340$, $690$
Which block's prices contain an outlier? Explain your answer.
development.solution_text:
Block A: $305, 320, 340, 355, 370, 390$
Block B: $312, 318, 325, 331, 340, 690$
In Block A each price is at most $20$ above the one before, so no price sits far from the rest.
Block B contains the outlier $690$, which is $350$ above the next highest price.

mastery.solution_text:
$22, 22, 24, 24, 26, 26, 26, 40$
Seven of the eight temperatures lie between $22^{\circ}$C and $26^{\circ}$C, so there is a cluster from $22^{\circ}$C to $26^{\circ}$C.
There is a gap between $26^{\circ}$C and $40^{\circ}$C, because no temperature was recorded in that interval.
The outlier is $40^{\circ}$C, recorded on day $6$, because it is much higher than the rest.

mastery.question_text: The prices of six houses in a street, in thousands of dollars, are $610$, $640$, $670$, $700$, $730$ and $760$. Ali says the house priced at $760$ must be the outlier because it is the most expensive. Explain why Ali is not correct.
mastery.solution_text:
$610, 640, 670, 700, 730, 760$
The prices go up in equal steps of $30$, so $760$ is only $30$ above the next highest price.
An outlier is a value much higher or much lower than all the others, not simply the largest value, so this dataset has no outlier.

$3, 4, 5, 6, 11, 12, 13, 25$
There is a cluster of four heights from $3$ m to $6$ m, and a second cluster of three heights from $11$ m to $13$ m.
There are gaps between $6$ m and $11$ m and between $13$ m and $25$ m, because no tree has a height in either interval.
The outlier is $25$ m, because it stands alone far above both clusters.
